chunks: It was narrated in it from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)
I have received [the amount], and praise be to Allah, and I have noticed the expenses that were sent to you from it. May Allah forgive you and them their sins, and have mercy on us and you.

key_terms.الْوُجُوهَ: The expenses / the means / the ways
key_terms.قَبَضْتُ: I have received (referring to money or goods)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Jawad say regarding the receipt of funds and personal expenses in his epistle?
ai.summary: This epistle from Imam al-Jawad (a.s.) to his emissary highlights the spiritual dimension of financial stewardship, where personal expenditure is viewed as a means of expiating sins. It underscores the Shia concept of the Imam’s intercessory role, linking material transactions with divine mercy and forgiveness for both the sender and the receiver.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 305 - The following epistle was issued from Imam Jawad (a.s) about him:
Praise be to Allah, I have received the amount and noticed that you have borne some of the expenses yourself. Almighty Allah would forgive your and their sins and would be merciful to us and you.
